classification: paper design; no new-domain implementation or experimental result
central_problem: Preserve source-identifiable heterogeneous infrastructure evidence under replay/failure without false equivalence, and measure history storage, reconstruction and processing costs against simpler batch methods.

questions.question: Can typed identity, coverage and publication contracts preserve declared evidence under retry, disorder and partial failure?
questions.hypothesis: Clean and perturbed runs yield identical accepted logical histories under the declared failure model.
questions.acceptance: Zero unexplained mismatches; explicit source exclusions unchanged.
questions.refutation: Any lost legitimate occurrence, fabricated removal, conflicting identity or visible partial analytical state.

questions.question: How do lossless historical representations trade storage against exact reconstruction and query cost?
questions.hypothesis: At least one state representation meets the declared byte/query preference rule; null: none does.

acceptance.interpretation: engineering preference, not scientific law; every required query must qualify

questions.refutation: Incorrect reconstruction, insufficient saving, or any required query exceeding the registered bound rejects preference.

questions.question: How do real workload shape and delivery policy affect local processing cost and streaming utility relative to batch?
questions.hypothesis: RIS streaming can preserve evidence at the declared 1x physical replay target within limits; universal speed superiority is not hypothesized.

acceptance.capacity_target: 1x of the fixed measured collector-hour mean, physical load only

questions.refutation: Identity mismatch, budget breach, nonzero final lag or excessive drain fails capacity claim; report saturation/negative baseline outcomes.
